reason: The cited evidence discusses Cr2O3 passivation films in HEAs and stainless steels (E1, E3) and elemental dissolution in a HEA (E2), but none of it addresses oxide film formation, composition, or protective behavior on Q235 steel, nor does it support the specific claims about Fe2O3 versus Fe3O4 films.
premises: A dense, adherent Fe2O3-rich oxide film can form on Q235 steel during high-temperature annealing in air.
A dense Fe2O3 film acts as a barrier to ion transport and elemental dissolution during molten salt exposure at 700–900 °C.
A porous or mixed Fe2O3/Fe3O4 film leads to accelerated corrosion in molten salt.
The identity and integrity of the passivation film is the crucial factor governing corrosion resistance, as observed in HEAs and stainless steels.
